title: Grateful Dead Live at The Eureka Municipal Auditorium on 1968-01-20

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of an explosive early‑68 set highlighted by a jazzy Clementine, incendiary Spanish Jam and the New Potato > Born Cross‑Eyed sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording is a surprisingly pristine sound‑board source for a 1968 tape, with listeners repeatedly noting its crispness despite the inevitable analog hiss. Musically the show is revered for Garcia’s swinging lead on Clementine, a scorching Spanish Jam, and the rare New Potato > Born Cross‑Eyed transition, all backed by tight rhythm work and vivid organ textures.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 50 enthusiastic reviews praise both the performance (standout songs, energetic playing) and the audio quality (crisp soundboard). The few minor complaints are about song length, not overall enjoyment, yielding a near‑excellent rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, crisp mix with typical analog hiss; vocals low but not detrimental. Reviewers repeatedly call it one of the best‑sounding early ’68 tapes.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Energetic early‑68 set praised for seamless transitions—Clementine into New Potato, then into Born Cross‑Eyed and Spanish Jam—creating a tight, swinging arc despite some very short jams (Caution, Dark Star).

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s jazzy lead on Clementine and soaring tone in the Spanish Jam are highlighted as among his best early work.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s bass leads (especially at the start of Caution) receive strong praise; his interplay with the organ is noted.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ work is described as “top form” and essential to the texture; a brief debate about whether it’s Pigpen or Tom Constanten, but overall very positive.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann are lauded for delivering some of their finest early‑68 drumming, driving the high‑energy jams.
